issue_paraphrase: On Python 3.12, code that contains an f-string with escaped (doubled) curly braces is linted wrongly: the step that replaces string contents with filler text miscounts the escaped braces and hands downstream plugins a garbled, misaligned version of the line. A flake8 plugin that reports content extracted from the linted line (for example a logging-call or formatting check) therefore prints a corrupted snippet, with filler characters where the escaped braces should be, instead of the actual code.
fix_summary: In FileProcessor (src/flake8/processor.py), when replacing the content of an FSTRING_MIDDLE token with 'x's on 3.12, compensate for escaped braces: extend the replacement text and the end column by the number of '{' plus '}' characters in the token, because each escaped brace occupies two raw source columns but only one token character.
notes: flake8 7.1.x-dev era (Aug 2024): the entire modern test suite runs on Python 3.12, the flake8 CLI works, no network needed. Gold test uses only the stdlib + pytest (the local-plugin fixture it wires up reads from tmpdir). Runs in <0.1s at 1 CPU. pytest.ini sets filterwarnings=error; the gold test does not trip it. Do not force pycodestyle>=2.13: the era's pycodestyle 2.12.x produces the clean failure shown above while 2.14.x makes the same failing test instead surface a different 'plugin code does not match' critical-error path (also a failure, but confusing).

issue_paraphrase: On Python 3.10 and newer, flake8 crashes with an AttributeError instead of reporting a syntax error when it checks a Python file that fails to parse. Python 3.10 appended extra ending-position fields to the information attached to SyntaxError; flake8 assumes the old layout, reads a bare integer where it expects the failing source text, and dies calling string methods on it, so users never see the E999 report for the faulty line.
fix_summary: In FileChecker._extract_syntax_information (src/flake8/checker.py), only apply the 1-indexed column adjustment when the SyntaxError detail tuple has the pre-3.10 4-element shape (len(token) == 4), and read the physical line at the stable index token[3] instead of the last element, so the new 6-element tuple on 3.10+ is left untouched.
notes: flake8 3.9.2-era code (Aug 2021) verified on Python 3.12.13 / bench-base:python-3.12. IMPORTANT: in this era the flake8 CLI cannot even start on Python 3.12 for an unrelated reason -- flake8._compat hardwires stdlib importlib.metadata on py3.8+, and Python 3.12's entry_points() returns EntryPoints with no .get, so plugin loading dies with AttributeError: 'EntryPoints' object has no attribute 'get' (observed directly with flake8 --version at both parent and fix). The gold test only calls the staticmethod FileChecker._extract_syntax_information and is fully deterministic; author the task so the model reproduces via pytest / the unit call, never via the CLI. No network, <0.1s at 1 CPU. pytest.ini sets filterwarnings=error; no warnings raised.

issue_paraphrase: flake8 aborts with a FileNotFoundError traceback before checking anything when it runs in an environment whose HOME variable points to a directory that does not exist -- for example the 'nobody' user in a Debian container with HOME=/nonexistent. The config-file discovery step stats the home directory without checking that it exists, so such an account cannot run flake8 at all; it should fall back to ordinary config discovery and lint normally.
fix_summary: In _find_config_file (src/flake8/options/config.py), wrap the os.stat of the expanded home path in try/except OSError (FileNotFoundError/PermissionError/etc.) and treat an un-stat-able home the same as an unset one (home_stat = None), so discovery continues.
notes: flake8 5.0.4-era code (Aug 2022) verified on Python 3.12.13 / bench-base:python-3.12. Same era caveat as the #1372 entry: the CLI of this era cannot start on Python 3.12 (stdlib importlib.metadata.entry_points() has no .get; observed the AttributeError with flake8 --version at this very commit), so the task must reproduce through the pytest gold test (or a direct call to flake8.options.config._find_config_file with expanduser patched to a missing path). The gold test mocks os.path.expanduser; no network, <0.1s at 1 CPU.
